newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's car scheme nets state 477 bln lire--study.
newsitem.headline: Italy's car scheme nets state 477 bln lire--study.

text.p: Italy's new car buying incentive scheme in the first five months of 1997 has benefitted the government some 477 billion lire, according to a study on Friday by car research body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP).

Italy started its car incentive scheme in January this year, financed by the government and car industry, whereby owners of cars 10 years old or more can scrap their vehicles in return for a price discount on a new car. The scheme is scheduled to run to the end of September.

Up to the end of May, the number of old cars traded in for scrapping under the scheme was 347,781 with a cost to the state of 574 billion lire. But value added tax and new car registration tax brought to the state 1.051 trillion lire, leaving a net benefit to the state of 477 billion lire.
CSP calculate the cost to the state of the scrapping scheme was 1.651 million lire per car.
